semantic_inputs: public provider-verified sigstore/cosign exact commit and README blob identity

milestone.name: mixed-origin finite certificate preserves trust scopes
milestone.revision: A finite proof-carrying rule can conjunct an own repository blob identity, a provider-verified external commit/file identity and a declared configuration without silently upgrading any premise. Positive MIXED_OK passes only with exact config/own identity/external verified exact-ref identity; independent flips to own SHA, external verification status, external file SHA, config or immutable-ref condition all reject.

mixed_origin_certificate.scope: identity/config finite decision over one own Git blob and one preexisting GitHub-provider-verified public commit/file

phase1_assessment.trust_scope_rule: Conjunction inherits the intersection/conjunction of scopes and never promotes provider assertion to independent cryptography or declared config to ambient observation.

negative_evidence: Provider-verified signed commit evidence cannot be replaced by mutable branch identity.
Signed external file identity does not imply text semantic correctness without an explicit bounded parser/rule.
Mixed evidence does not enable fresh external signing or deployment side effects.

frontier.action: Test GitHub annotated signed tags as an immutable release anchor: locate a public tag object, inspect provider verification, and if verified bind its target commit/file identity. Record lightweight/unsigned tags as negatives.
Apply a bounded text rule to a file at an exact provider-verified signed commit, explicitly separating authenticity of identity from parsed content semantics.
Generalize the premise lattice into a role-local reusable certificate schema with explicit origin, immutable anchor, evidence pointer, admitted operations and inherited scope.

exact_next_action: Inspect official GitHub release/tag data for sigstore/cosign or another security-focused public repository. Resolve an exact tag ref. If it points to an annotated tag object, fetch that object and require verification.verified=true and reason=valid before admitting it; then follow only its exact target commit and fetch one file identity at that target. If the tag is lightweight or unsigned, record the failure without using tag/release message semantics. No signing, Actions, Cosign verification or hosted job.
chronology_note: Logical revision 153 and repository commit ancestry are authoritative. r152 already recorded that several earlier artifact filename timestamps were estimated; no semantic claim depends on those nominal times.
termination: intermediate Phase-1 checkpoint; global completion false; frontier nonempty
